macro.narrative: The current macro backdrop—expanding ISM manufacturing and services indices, robust new orders, an upward‑sloping yield curve, low VIX, and a bullish S&P—creates a favorable environment for Charter’s broadband, video and mobile services. Demand for high‑speed connectivity and entertainment is likely to rise, supporting subscriber growth and higher average revenue per user. Pricing power may improve as consumers are willing to pay for premium services, while input costs remain relatively stable. Capital expenditures will be needed to expand fiber and 5G infrastructure, but financing costs are moderate due to the yield curve shape.

implications.why: Expansion in ISM new orders signals stronger corporate and consumer spending on connectivity, boosting Charter's subscriber acquisition prospects.
With higher demand and low VIX, consumers are more willing to pay for premium broadband and mobile plans, allowing Charter to maintain or increase ARPU.
Commodity prices for fiber and equipment may rise modestly, but the upward yield curve suggests moderate inflation, keeping input cost pressure limited.
Macro expansion supports Charter’s fiber and 5G rollout plans, justifying higher capex to capture growing market share.
The upward‑sloping yield curve indicates slightly higher long‑term borrowing rates, increasing debt servicing costs for Charter’s recent acquisitions.
Stronger demand improves cash conversion, reducing days sales outstanding and improving working capital efficiency.
